digest.en: Alice Huang remains barred from Singapore despite insufficient evidence of offences. Meanwhile, Prabowo consolidates power as Gibran’s exit weakens Widodo’s grip. These moves signal shifting alliances in the region.
digest.hi: ईरान ने आज न्यूयॉर्क में अमेरिकी दूतावास को चेतावनी दी कि किसी भी अमेरिकी हमले का जवाब दस गुना अधिक घातक होगा। इसी बीच अबू धाबी में रूस-यूक्रेन समझौते की संभावनाओं पर चर्चा चल रही है, जहाँ दोनों पक्ष शर्तों पर झुंझलाते दिखे।

articles.title: Alice Huang barred from re-entering Singapore; insufficient evidence she committed offences in
articles.summary: Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country. The Ministry of Home Affairs stated there was insufficient evidence she committed offences. Officials emphasized the nation will not allow misuse of its business environment for fraud or dishonest practices. "Singapore is committed to upholding our reputation as a trusted and reliable business hub. We will not allow companies or individuals to misuse Singapore's business environment to engage in fraud or dishonest practices," the Ministry of Home Affairs said.

articles.title: Arrests, Attacks, And A Familiar Kremlin Refrain
articles.summary: US, Ukraine, and Russia held trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. Negotiations focused on broad security questions while deep gaps remained over Donbas territorial control. Russia continued military attacks on Ukraine and domestic crackdowns on citizens during the discussions. At the first US-Ukraine-Russia negotiations since February, talk turns to broad questions of security while wide gaps remain over core issues such as territorial control in the Donbas.

articles.title: Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the history of ‘sexpionage’
articles.summary: Intelligence agencies often target key individuals to compromise them. This involves damaging reputations or creating situations where sensitive information might be disclosed. Such tactics aim to gain access to data adversaries do not want shared. A large portion of intelligence work is focused on collecting information your competitor or adversary does not want you to have. But another key focus of intelligence is on compromising key individuals.

articles.title: Prabowo gains upper hand as Gibran’s exit weakens Widodo’s grip
articles.summary: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned, shifting power dynamics. President Prabowo Subianto gained the upper hand as Jokowi lost his direct presence in the administration. Jokowi had previously helped carry Prabowo to the presidency in 2024. Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka’s resignation may mark a turning point in the balance of power between President Prabowo Subianto and his predecessor, Joko Widodo.

articles.title: Amish Shah, Pia Dandiya join centrist New Democratic Coalition
articles.summary: Amish Shah and Pia Dandiya joined the New Democratic Coalition. This centrist caucus operates within the Democratic party. The separate progressive caucus has over 100 members and is led by Texas Congressman Greg Casar. The other prominent caucus within the Democratic party – the progressives – has over 100 members and is led by Texas Congressman Greg Casar with lawmakers Ilhan Omar, Pramila Jayapal and Ro Khanna as members.

articles.title: Democrats preview plan to roll back US-Israel defense integration
articles.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen led a group of Democrats in demanding the repeal of US-Israel military integration efforts. The lawmakers warned the bipartisan initiative threatens American national security. Van Hollen is considering a bid for Senate majority leader against Chuck Schumer. Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is considering a bid for Senate majority leader against Sen. Chuck Schumer, led a group of Democratic lawmakers on November 10 in demanding that congressional leaders scrap a bipartisan effort to more closely integrate the American and Israeli militaries, warning the initiative would threaten US national security and risk further [] The post Democrats preview plan to ro.

articles.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case
articles.summary: Argentina's lawyer Marcelo Kohen mocked Britain's sovereignty claims in a Hamburg tribunal hearing. He argued the UK should not act as a colonial power. Kohen rejected the historic doctrine of British maritime dominance over Falklands waters. Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceansBritain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal. Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently belie.

articles.title: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
articles.summary: Ecuadorian journalist Tomás Beltrán was shot dead while parking his car in Calceta. The killing highlights deteriorating security conditions in the country. Gang warfare over drug routes has made the Pacific coastline a key flashpoint. Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violentTomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead. Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over d.

articles.title: From Japan to Rwanda, early warnings are saving lives – but millions remain unprotected
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres stated that early warning systems are saving lives globally. However, millions remain unprotected as warnings fail to reach them. He urged the international community to ensure every person on Earth is covered by these systems by the end of 2027. Early warning systems are saving lives across the globe, but for millions of people the warning never arrives, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said on Wednesday, urging the world to protect every person on Earth by the end of 2027.

articles.title: After 48 years patrolling the Blue Line, UN peacekeepers prepare exit
articles.summary: UN peacekeepers are preparing to exit southern Lebanon after 48 years of patrolling the Blue Line. Hostilities have decreased following a June agreement between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel. Communities report the situation remains volatile and difficult for those attempting to rebuild their lives. The situation in southern Lebanon remains volatile and extremely difficult for communities trying to rebuild their lives, UN peacekeepers based there report, despite a significant decrease in hostilities following an agreement in June between the United States, Lebanon and Israel.

articles.title: China’s tech export boom is hiding a weakening economy
articles.summary: China's annual trade surplus surpassed one trillion dollars despite US tariff pressures. Imports also hit their highest level since 2021. The figures suggest the economy remains resilient. Beijing continues to export heavily while domestic consumption recovers slowly. NEW YORK. A week after US voters rebuked Donald Trump’s Republican Party, China delivered a stinging reminder that his presidency is going awry from all directions.

articles.title: Wartime memory shows China-Russia ties far from ‘limitless’
articles.summary: China and Russia have aligned their official memories of the Second World War for over a decade. They stage joint commemorations and coordinate remembrance dates. This memory alliance reveals their ties are far from limitless despite shared narratives. For more than a decade, China and Russia have sought to align their official memories of the Second World War. They have staged prominent joint commemorations and military parades, while also coordinating remembrance dates and harmonizing their official discourses about the war.

articles.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK
articles.summary: Argentina told the Hamburg tribunal that Britain’s approval of the Sea Lion oil project deepened the Falklands sovereignty dispute. The legal clash marks a historic confrontation over drilling rights in the North Falkland basin. The dispute traces back to the war four decades ago. Sea Lion project in the North Falkland basin threatens to deepen sovereignty disputeArgentina has told an international tribunal that Britain’s approval of oil drilling off the Falkland Islands has dramatically deepened a sovereignty dispute that led to war four decades ago. At the start of an historic legal clash at the Hamburg-based International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (Itlos), an Argent.

articles.title: Moscow Police Detain Hundreds Of Youths, Pressure Those Of Military Age Into Service
articles.summary: Moscow police detained hundreds of youths, including children, during a raid on an alternative gathering. Detainees reported beatings and denial of basic needs. Adults received draft notices or faced pressure to sign army contracts. Police labeled the action a preventive operation. Hundreds, including children, were detained in a raid on an alternative youth gathering in central Moscow. Detainees reported beatings and being denied water and toilets.

articles.title: Ukraine, Russia Negotiators Conclude First Day Of US-Led Peace Talks As Europe Seeks Role
articles.summary: Ukrainian and Russian negotiators concluded the first day of US-brokered peace talks. The two-day session aims to address Moscow’s ongoing war on Ukraine. It remains unclear if any tangible progress was made during the initial session. Ukrainian and Russian negotiators wrapped up the first of two days of US-brokered talks aimed at untangling Moscow's nearly 5-year-old all-out war on Ukraine, though it was unclear what progress there had been, if any.

articles.title: IOM urges wider surveillance beyond formal routes in DR Congo
articles.summary: The International Organization for Migration urged broader surveillance beyond formal routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases were detected along transit routes since the outbreak began six months ago. The agency highlighted the need to monitor movement outside standard health checkpoints. Seventy-one confirmed Ebola cases have been detected along transit routes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) since the outbreak began almost six months ago, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Nearly 64,000 flee Nigeria for Niger where a humanitarian crisis is deepening
articles.summary: UNHCR reported 64,000 people fled northern Nigeria for Niger this year. Several hundred also left for Benin. Violence in the region is deepening a humanitarian crisis. Host countries are struggling to cope with the sudden influx of displaced residents. Violence in northern Nigeria is fueling a growing humanitarian crisis across the whole region: 64,000 have fled to neighbouring Niger and several hundred have left for Benin since the start of the year, as host countries struggle to cope, the UN’s refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Fact-checking site’s entire newsroom jailed as assault on press freedom widens
articles.summary: Six journalists from the Egyptian fact-checking site Matsadash remain in detention. The UN human rights office confirmed their continued imprisonment. This incident highlights a widening assault on press freedom. The government faces criticism for targeting independent media operations. Six journalists who make up the entire newsroom of the Egyptian fact-checking website Matsadash remain in detention, the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said on Tuesday, warning of proliferating assaults on press freedom by the Government.

articles.title: South Sudan’s first elections loom amid rising violence
articles.summary: South Sudan faces its first national elections in six weeks as violence escalates. The Security Council meets in New York to demand credible polls. Civilians continue to suffer from fighting, hunger, and displacement. With South Sudan just six weeks away from its first national elections since independence, the Security Council meets in New York Tuesday amid deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence.

articles.title: First ‘suicide’ drone attacks, now long-range strikes are the norm
articles.summary: UNICEF warns that drones and drought are closing in on Sudan. Attackers now use long-range drones traveling up to 1,500 kilometers. These strikes target critical infrastructure across the country. Drones and drought are “closing in” on Sudan, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF, said on Tuesday, describing unprecedented attacks on the country’s infrastructure including by drones travelling up to 1,500 kilometres before hitting their target.

articles.title: Climate crisis could push 141 million more women into extreme poverty
articles.summary: Over one billion women and girls live in climate hotspots. High hazard exposure combines with insecure jobs and gender inequality. The crisis could push 141 million more into extreme poverty. More than one in three women and girls worldwide – roughly 1.5 billion – live in so-called “climate hotspots”, where high exposure to hazards such as cyclones and droughts combine with insecure jobs and deep gender inequality.

articles.title: Europe's Fruitless Search For A Ukraine Peace Envoy; EU Safeguards For Montenegro
articles.summary: The EU cannot agree on a single envoy for Russia-Ukraine peace talks. Meanwhile, Montenegro faces potential safeguards upon joining the bloc. RFE/RL Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak analyzes both issues in this week's briefing. In this week's briefing, RFE/RL Europe Editor Rikard Jozwiak is drilling down on two issues: why the EU cannot agree on an envoy for Russia-Ukraine peace talks and what safeguards Montenegro could face when it joins the bloc.

articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China
articles.summary: Two Uyghurs face deportation from Thailand to China. Activists warn they will face torture and enslavement. Bangkok previously sent forty Uyghurs back last year. Human rights groups urge Thai authorities to halt the transfers. Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minorityThe deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back. Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghu.

articles.title: The View from Eritrea
articles.summary: Giulia Paravicini reports from Asmara, Eritrea's capital. She details daily life in the isolated nation. The piece examines leadership strategies amid regional instability. Tensions with Ethiopia continue to shape the country's foreign policy decisions. This week on The Horn, Alan speaks with Reuters journalist Giulia Paravicini about her recent reporting trip to Eritrea’s capital, Asmara, what she learned about life in the isolated country and its leadership’s calculations amid regional turmoil and mounting tensions with Ethiopia.

articles.title: On Our Radar
articles.summary: Crisis Group analysts review global conflict hotspots. The weekly brief highlights under-reported trends and major developments. Field experts explain why specific crises matter. The report offers recommendations for addressing emerging geopolitical risks. On Our Radar scans conflicts and crises around the globe every week and features some of the hotspots Crisis Group’s analysts are closely watching. Whether an under-reported trend or a headline-grabbing development, our field experts explain why it matters or what should be done.

articles.title: होर्मुज स्ट्रेट में बर्बाद हुआ 40 लाख बैरल तेल, समुद्री बारूदी सुरंगों का शिकार बने दो जहाज

articles.title: नॉर्वे की पत्रकार हेले ने किया वीजा रद्द होने का दावा: कांग्रेस के भारत समिट में लेना था हिस्सा
articles.summary: नॉर्वेजियन पत्रकार हेले लिंग ने दावा किया कि भारत में उनके वीजा को रद्द कर दिया गया। वह कांग्रेस पार्टी के भारत समिट में भाग लेने के लिए आए थे। वीजा रद्द होने की वजह से वह समिट में शामिल नहीं हो पाए। नॉर्वे की पत्रकार हेले ने किया वीजा रद्द होने का दावा: कांग्रेस के भारत समिट में लेना था हिस्सा।
